name: Pluchea

project_scope.note: Both species canonical in 2026-10-17 manifest. P. camphorata keeps user-approved UNRESOLVED range exception and exclusion from native metrics; P. odorata is provisional. No new installation or range decision.

recognition.where_to_look_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: inspect alternate leaf nodes, side-light the stem for cobwebby arachnose hairs, then photograph the entire flowering-branch arrangement. Finally measure three mature involucres in profile. Pink heads and petioles alone cannot distinguish these species.
priority: flat/rounded corymbiform versus more paniculiform head arrays
involucre shape and size for close confirmation
shared_morphology: Alternate leaves with glandular surfaces; petiolate or sessile depending on species.
Heads are disciform composites in corymbiform or paniculiform arrays, each with a cup of phyllaries (involucre).
Use mature involucre width, stem hairs and branch architecture together; odor and flower color are secondary.
overlap_cautions: Both species can have petioles: petiole presence alone is not diagnostic.
Mature involucre heights overlap at 5–6 mm; compare widths on multiple heads.
A cropped branch can hide paniculiform versus layered corymbiform architecture.
Stem hairs require adequate light/magnification; unclear hairs should be unscored.
FNA notes occasional hybrids; discordant intermediates need taxonomy review.

quick_split: P. camphorata — leaves clearly petiolate; stems usually closely arachnose; many small heads arranged in a paniculiform system of rounded-convex corymbiform clusters on ascending bracteate branches.
P. odorata — leaves sessile or petiolate; stems not arachnose; head arrays more directly corymbiform, flat-topped to rounded and often layered.
local_confusers: Heterotheca subaxillaris may share the camphorweed common-name problem but has conspicuous yellow ray florets.
Conoclinium has opposite leaves rather than the alternate Pluchea pattern.

rows.caution: Verify at 10–20× with side light; glandular hairs also occur.
Height overlaps; 4 mm width is boundary.

rows.camphorata: Paniculiform; rounded corymbiform clusters on ascending bracteate branches
rows.odorata: Corymbiform, flat to rounded, often layered

anatomy_lessons.title: 1 · Find the leaf node
anatomy_lessons.plain: Follow the leaf to where it joins the stem. The stalk is the petiole.
anatomy_lessons.look_here: Matched attached mid-stem nodes with a ruler.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Both are alternate; P. odorata can also be petiolate.

anatomy_lessons.title: 2 · Examine stem hairs
anatomy_lessons.plain: Arachnose means fine cobweb-like hairs; gland dots are different.
anatomy_lessons.look_here: Same stem zone side-lit at 10–20× on both species.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: P. camphorata usually closely arachnose; P. odorata not arachnose.

anatomy_lessons.title: 3 · Follow the flowering branches
anatomy_lessons.plain: Look at the central flowering axis and where the side branches start.
anatomy_lessons.look_here: Whole distal flowering branch, uncropped, matched scale.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Ascending paniculiform branches versus often layered corymbiform clusters.

anatomy_lessons.title: 4 · Measure the phyllary cup
anatomy_lessons.plain: The small overlapping bracts beneath a flower head form the involucre.
anatomy_lessons.look_here: Three mature heads in side view with a millimeter ruler; inner and outer bracts.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: P. camphorata 3–4 mm wide; P. odorata 4–8(–10) mm; lengths overlap.

comparison_cards.title: Stem hairs and leaf nodes
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Appressed arachnose hairs on the stem
comparison_cards.separator: Usually arachnose P. camphorata versus non-arachnose P. odorata; both may have petioles.

comparison_cards.title: Flowering-array architecture
comparison_cards.separator: P. camphorata paniculiform versus P. odorata often layered corymbiform; cropped clusters overlap.

comparison_cards.title: Mature involucre dimensions
comparison_cards.separator: P. camphorata 4–6 × 3–4 mm versus P. odorata 5–6 × 4–8(–10) mm; width 4 mm and height overlap.
